'''Sandy Wible''' (also '''Will "Sandy" Wible''') was Decipher's official online network representative in the Premiere era and later a Product Development game designer.

* [[Nysad]] — Sandy Wible

== Decipher ==

In January 1996 he posted a SWCCG rarity list to Usenet as "Official Online Network Representative for Decipher Inc." with the Genie address used for Decipher's online presence.

Chuck Kallenbach later recalled that Decipher needed an internet representative on the Genie boards; Wible won the role over Kallenbach, then invited Kallenbach to playtest SWCCG.<ref name="flashback">[http://www.theforce.net/ccg/flashback/article.asp Flashback: interview with Chuck Kallenbach], TheForce.Net. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010072858/http://www.theforce.net/ccg/flashback/article.asp Internet Archive]</ref>

Radio Free Decipher broadcast 25 (17 September 1999) interviewed "Product Development's Sandy Wible" on fall 1999 CCG news.<ref name="rfd25" /> In that episode Carol Wisely traced the succession of Rebel Base Leader / Jedi Master online-rules accounts. She placed Wible after Tom Braunlich ("Answer Man") and Jerry Darcy as an early Rebel Base Leader / first Jedi Master.

== Jedi Knights TCG ==
Wible did additional design on the [[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]] (2001). As Decipher's technical manager he coordinated its production.<ref name="jkrules">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt ''Jedi Knights'' Trading Card Game rulebook (credits)], Decipher (2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010820125115/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/rules/jediknightsrules.txt Internet Archive]</ref><ref name="jkpersonae">[http://www.decipher.com/jediknights/designdiary/personae.html Design Diary: Dramatis personae], decipher.com (2000–2001). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20010224092942/http://www.decipher.com:80/jediknights/designdiary/personae.html Internet Archive]</ref>
